resources.string: Install DeskLink Host on your Windows PC, then tap “Add PC” while this phone is on the same Wi-Fi.
Away from home, DeskLink reaches your PC over mobile data when the PC\'s router allows it. The DeskLink menu on the PC (tray icon) says whether it does.

The PC\'s router doesn\'t let DeskLink open the way in. Turn on UPnP in the router\'s settings, then on the PC turn \"Allow access over mobile data\" off and on again (DeskLink menu, next to the clock).
The PC\'s internet company shares one address between many homes (CGNAT), so mobile data can\'t reach it. You can ask them for a public IP address.
It may still work over IPv6 if the router lets incoming IPv6 connections in (look for the IPv6 firewall in its settings).

Control resumes automatically when the normal desktop is back.

Trackpad mode
• Drag one finger: move the pointer
• Let go while moving: the pointer glides on (touch to stop it)
• Tap: click · Double tap: double-click
• Tap with two fingers: right-click
• Tap with three fingers: middle-click
• Swipe with two fingers: scroll (let go while moving and it keeps scrolling; touch to stop it)
• Touch and hold, then drag: drag (or double-tap and drag). A ring at the pointer shows when the hold takes. To go further, put another finger down and lift the first
• Pinch: zoom
• Swipe up / down with three fingers: show / hide the keyboard

Direct touch mode
• Tap: click where you touch
• Touch and hold: right-click
• Drag one finger: drag
• Two fingers: scroll · Pinch: zoom

Shortcut bar (above the keyboard)
• Edit, Ctrl Alt, Esc Tab, ← ↑ ↓ →: tap to show those keys, tap again to hide them
• Ctrl, Shift, Alt: tap = stays pressed until you tap it again; touch and hold = pressed while held (Settings → Keyboard can make them work only while held)
• Win: a tap is a press (it opens Start); touch and hold = pressed while held (Win + a key)

Buttons at the bottom right
• Keyboard: show / hide the phone keyboard
• Shortcut keys: keep the shortcut bar on screen (tap again to hide it)

Top bar
• It stays until you hide it with ˄; the ˅ at the top brings it back
• The mode button switches trackpad → direct touch → Gaming mode; touch and hold it to pick one, or a gaming profile
• With more than one screen on the PC: the two-screens button shows them all at once (pinch to look closer; tap it again for one screen), the screen-with-an-arrow button goes to the next one
• ⋮: send files to the PC or get one from it, pick a screen, Ctrl+Alt+Del, lock the PC, Task Manager

Gaming mode
• An on-screen gamepad: holding a button holds its key or mouse button on the PC
• The stick (DualShock) steers smoothly; Settings → Pad type → Digital gives the D-pad instead
• Drag between the buttons to move the pointer; in a game that hides the pointer, it turns the camera
• Each profile has its own name and buttons: Settings → Profiles…

Settings (⋮ → Settings): pointer speed, keyboard, Gaming mode, picture, clipboard
